workingOn.title: Agent workflows at Lightfield
workingOn.summary: Lately I’ve been working on APIs, agent tools, and the task and review workflows behind Lightfield’s CRM.

question.prompt: How much of an agent's intermediate state should a person have to see?
question.currentView: I think people should be able to see proposals, ownership, and state when the work has real consequences.
question.counterargument: Good defaults, easy rollback, and a useful activity log might matter more than seeing every step.
question.wouldChange: I’m curious which controls people actually use once rollback is reliable and the history is clear.

changedMyMind.previous: I thought chat was mostly a temporary way to show off what models could do.
changedMyMind.changed: Longer-running tasks made it hard to ignore the gap between a good conversation and work that needs to last.
changedMyMind.current: I still think chat is useful while intent is taking shape. The actual workflow just needs to live somewhere sturdier.

selections.whyNow: It’s still growing on me. That feels more honest than pretending I had an instant verdict.
I came back to it after years away and heard it differently.
I keep thinking about the way competence and loneliness sit next to each other.
I keep thinking about how much the pacing and the room shaped the meal.
